t:
(a) Administration of Authority by Secretaries of Military Departments.—Subsection (a) of section 2583 of title 10, United States Code, is amended—
        (1) by striking “Secretary of Defense may” and inserting “Secretary of the military department concerned may”; and 
        (2) by striking “the Department of Defense” and inserting “such military department”.  
    (b) Authority to Make Dogs Available for Adoption Before End of Useful Working Life.—Such subsection is further amended by striking “at the end” and all that follows and inserting “, unless the dog has been determined to be unsuitable for adoption under subsection (b), under circumstances as follows:“(1) At the end of the dog’s useful working life.“(2) Before the end of the dog’s useful working life, if such Secretary, in such Secretary’s discretion, determines that unusual or extraordinary circumstances justify making the dog available for adoption before that time.“(3) When the dog is otherwise excess to the needs of such military department.”. 
    (c) Clarification of Reporting Requirement.—Subsection (f) of such section is amended by inserting “of Defense” after “Secretary”. 
    (d) Conforming and Clerical Amendments.—The heading of such section, and the item relating to such section in the table of sections at the beginning of chapter 153 of such title, are each amended by striking the last six words.

fable.w: The section shifts authority over military working dog adoptions from the Secretary of Defense to the military department Secretaries and lets them decide, in their own discretion, when a dog may be adopted. The tempting reading is that adoption by outside persons or the reporting requirement amounts to participation, but adopting a dog is akin to applying for a benefit and the report goes to Congress, which is inside the federal government. There is no rulemaking, public comment, hearing, advisory body, outside consultation, or right to sue.
fable.s: determines that unusual or extraordinary circumstances justify making the dog available for adoption before that time

qwen_block.w: This section amends statutory language to shift authority from the Secretary of Defense to the Secretaries of specific military departments. All actors involved (Secretaries of Defense and military departments) are inside the federal government. There is no requirement for consultation with, or participation by, any outside parties such as the public, states, or private organizations.
qwen_block.s: (a) Administration of Authority by Secretaries of Military Departments.—Subsection (a) of section 2583 of title 10, United States Code, is amended— (1) by striking “Secretary of Defense may” and inserting “Secretary of the military department concerned may”; and (2) by striking “the Department of Defense” and inserting “such military department”.

opus.w: The section moves the dog-adoption power from the Secretary of Defense to the Secretaries of the military departments and lets them make dogs available early, at their own discretion. No one outside the federal government is consulted or allowed to comment, object or sue. Adopting a dog is like applying for a benefit, not taking part in the decision, and the reporting change is a technical fix that stays inside the government.
opus.s: if such Secretary, in such Secretary’s discretion, determines that unusual or extraordinary circumstances justify making the dog available for adoption before that time.
opus.b:
1. **Thinking it through.** The tempting reading is that letting outside people adopt military working dogs, together with the "reporting requirement," involves people outside the government. That reading fails on both points. Adopting a dog is like applying for a benefit, and the adopter has no part in the decision itself. The Secretary of the military department decides alone whether "unusual or extraordinary circumstances" justify an early adoption. The reporting change only adds "of Defense" after "Secretary," which is a technical fix. Any such report would stay inside the federal government. The section has no consultation, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue.

2. **Label.**

qwen_chat.w: This section primarily amends internal administrative authorities within the Department of Defense, shifting decision-making power from the Secretary of Defense to the Secretaries of individual military departments. It also clarifies a reporting requirement to the Secretary of Defense. There is no requirement for the federal government to consult with or coordinate with outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) before making a decision. The mention of dog adoption is an administrative procedure for disposing of government property, not a participatory process in the definition's sense.
qwen_chat.s: (a) Administration of Authority by Secretaries of Military Departments.—Subsection (a) of section 2583 of title 10, United States Code, is amended— (1) by striking “Secretary of Defense may” and inserting “Secretary of the military department concerned may”; and (2) by striking “the Department of Defense” and inserting “such military department”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that allowing dogs to be adopted by the public constitutes "participation" because it involves interaction with outside parties (the adopters). However, the definition explicitly excludes "applications for benefits" and focuses on consultation or coordination *before* a federal decision is made. The adoption process is an administrative outcome, not a participatory decision-making process where the public advises or influences the government's policy or regulatory choices. Furthermore, the section primarily deals with internal administrative changes (shifting authority between Secretaries) and reporting requirements to Congress (which is inside the government).
